paragraphs: Rav Huna bar Livai: Ein Yaakov, according to Hyman. The consulted [Berakhot 55b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.55b.3) has simply Rav Huna.[^3]
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi is called bar Livai; see his entry. Rabbah bar Livai, [Pesachim 40b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.40b.3).

notes.text: Ein Yaakov is the cited reading for Huna bar Livai; the ordinary reading lacks the patronym. The list retains Yehoshua ben Levi’s separate use of bar Livai.

The consulted Berakhot 27b directly names Rav Dimi bar Livai. The exact Ein Yaakov reading for Huna bar Livai was not independently inspected here; the collective list does not establish one shared father for all its names.

[Seder HaDorot 1001](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1001&lang=en) likewise reports “Rav Huna bar Livai” as a reading of Ein Yaakov and “Rav Huna” as the Bavli reading. [Seder HaDorot 1385](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1385&lang=en) lists Chana with this patronymic at [Sanhedrin 108b:21](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.108b.21), a separate notice.
